Easiest Chicken Curry 🍛

Method:-

- to the chicken we will add 1 teaspoon each of haldi powder or turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt and a little bit of oil.
- Massage it all in well and keep it aside to marinate for at least 15 to 20 minutes.

-in a Kadhai add 3-4 tablespoon of oil. 
-once the oil is hot we will add 1 teaspoon each of cumin seeds or zeera, 7-8 corns of black pepper, 6 dried red chillies, 7-8 cloves of peeled garlic, 1 cinnamon stick and a bay leaf.
The spice tolerance depends on your taste. You can adjust the amount of red chillies as per your wish and will.

-when everything looks and smells toasty we will add in the onions and cook it with salt till they are brown.
we have taken 4 medium to big onions for half a kg chicken. 

-half way through the process add 1 tablespoon full of ginger and garlic paste.
-Mix it with the onions and then add 1 teaspoon each of red chilli powder, zeera powder or cumin powder, dhaniya or coriander powder, garam masala and Kashmiri Lal mirch.
-Mix it all well and add a little bit of water to help the onions caramelise.

-when the onions are caramelised and mushy we will add out marinated chicken to it.
-We will stir it a couple of time before putting the lid on and cooking it on medium flame for 15-17 minutes. 
-In the end we will add a couple of chopped green chillies with coriander.
You can totally avoid the green chillies if you can’t tolerate very spicy food.
-serve however, UMAMI.

🔥 Bachelor Chicken Peratal — quick, simple and full of flavour!
🍗 A spicy homemade masala + crispy roasted onions = the perfect bachelor-friendly chicken!

🍗 Bachelor Chicken Peratal Recipe

Ingredients (with measurements)

For Masala Paste:

Coriander seeds – 1 tbsp

Black pepper – 1 tsp

Cumin seeds – 1 tsp

Cinnamon – 1 small piece

Cloves – 2 -4 No's

Cardamom – 1

Kashmiri chilli powder – 1 tsp

Red chilli powder – ½ tsp

Turmeric powder – ¼ tsp

Salt – as needed

Ginger - 2 Inch

Garlic- 4 No's

Water – 2–3 tbsp (to grind)

For Chicken Peratal:

Chicken – 350g

Oil – 3 tbsp

Onion – 2 large, thinly sliced

---

Method

1. Grind the masala:
Add all the whole spices, chilli powders, turmeric and salt. Add a little water and grind into a smooth paste.

2. Marinate the chicken:
Coat the chicken with the masala paste and marinate for 30 minutes
(If you’re in a hurry, you can cook immediately.)

3. Roast the onions:
Heat oil in a pan and roast the sliced onions until golden brown and crispy.

4. Cook the chicken:
Add the marinated chicken to the roasted onions.
Cook on medium flame, cover and let it cook until the chicken turns soft and the masala thickens.
Once oil separates and the masala becomes dry, your Bachelor Chicken Peratal is ready!
